 Martirosyan defeats Carlsen on Day 3 in Budapest
 Friday, 13 Nov 2026 
 UTC +1 
 21:51 
 Share this post: 
 CHESS NEWS 
 Tags: 
 Total Chess World Championship Tour 
 Caruana extends his lead, and Vachier-Lagrave moves into clear first 
 Haik Martirosyan defeated Magnus Carlsen and took the outright lead in Group C on the third day of the Fast Classic group stage at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest. Andrew Hong also caused an upset by handing Group A leader Alireza Firouzja his first defeat of the group stage.
 Games 5 and 6 produced 10 decisive results from 24 encounters. Each player again faced the same opponent twice with colours reversed, with three points awarded for a win and one for a draw.
 After six games per player, all four groups have outright leaders. Firouzja heads Group A on eleven points, Fabiano Caruana leads Group B on fourteen, Martirosyan tops Group C on ten, and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave leads Group D on twelve.
 Firouzja strikes back after Hong claims his first win 
 Andrew Hong recorded his first Fast Classic victory of the event by defeating Alireza Firouzja with White in a complicated battle. Firouzja responded with a White win in the return game, creating an advantage and forcing favourable exchanges before securing the win. The three points apiece leave Firouzja on eleven and Hong on six.
 Jan-Krzysztof Duda and Levon Aronian drew both games. Duda remains second on nine points, two behind Firouzja, with Aronian on seven.
 Jorden van Foreest collected four points against Nodirbek Abdusattorov , winning their first encounter before drawing the return. Van Foreest moves to eight points, while Abdusattorov has five.
 Caruana stretches his lead to four points 
 Fabiano Caruana continued his unbeaten run by defeating Vincent Keymer with Black in their first game. Caruana gained the upper hand in the endgame and successfully converted his advantage. A draw in the return took Caruana to fourteen points from four wins and two draws, while Keymer finished the day on four.
 Le Quang Liem drew both games with Richard Rapport to reach ten points, four behind Caruana. Rapport moves to five.
 Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu and Vladislav Artemiev also drew twice. Their first encounter lasted 89 moves. Artemiev has five points and Praggnanandhaa four.
 Martirosyan beats Carlsen to seize the Group C lead 
 Haik Martirosyan produced the day’s standout result by inflicting Magnus Carlsen’s first Fast Classic defeat after four consecutive draws. Playing with White in the first game, Martirosyan launched a dangerous attack and eventually broke through to secure the victory. A draw in the return encounter gave Martirosyan four points from the pair and the outright Group C lead on ten. Carlsen has five.
 Shakhriyar Mamedyarov and Abhimanyu Mishra drew both encounters, taking them to seven and five points respectively.
 Anish Giri moved into second place on nine points after drawing his first game with Ian Nepomniachtchi and winning the return with White. Giri prevailed after a long battle, leaving Nepomniachtchi on seven.
 Shakhriyar Mamedyarov and Abhimanyu Mishra drew both encounters, taking them to seven and five points respectively.
 Vachier-Lagrave moves clear as Vaishali retaliates 
 Maxime Vachier-Lagrave won the direct encounter between the Group D leaders. After drawing his first game with Hans Moke Niemann , he built up sustained pressure with White in the return and converted the advantage. Vachier-Lagrave reaches twelve points, three clear of Niemann.
 Arjun Erigaisi joined Niemann on nine points after a win and a draw against Wesley So . Erigaisi came under pressure in the first game but turned the tables to secure the victory. The return was drawn, leaving So on four.
 Bibisara Assaubayeva and Vaishali Rameshbabu exchanged wins with White. Assaubayeva struck first, but Vaishali responded with an attacking victory of her own to claim her first Fast Classic win of the event. Assaubayeva moves to eight points and Vaishali to four.
 The Fast Classic group stage continues on Saturday, November 14, with Games 7 and 8. Four games remain for each player before the group standings determine places in the six knockout brackets.
 Text: Total Chess 
 Photos: Maria Emelianova and Michal Walusza

 About Total Chess 
 Total Chess is a global championship platform established to redefine elite competitive chess for the modern era. Developed by Norway Chess and approved by FIDE, the Total Chess World Championship Tour introduces a unified format that crowns the world’s ultimate champion by testing excellence across three disciplines: Fast Classical, Rapid and Blitz. The Tour will bring together the world’s top 24 men and women players to compete across four premier international events hosted in leading global cities. Designed to elevate the sport’s commercial appeal and fan engagement, Total Chess combines world-class competition with innovation, technology and immersive spectator experiences to create a new benchmark for professional chess.
 With a vision to make chess one of the world’s most engaging and commercially sustainable sports, Total Chess aims to expand the game’s global footprint, inspire the next generation of players, and connect millions of fans through a dynamic championship that celebrates intelligence, strategy and sporting excellence.
